identity.title: ALMA Spectral Survey of an Eruptive Young Star, V883 Ori (ASSAY). II. Freshly Sublimated Complex Organic Molecules in the Keplerian Disk

paper_type_evidence.quote: based on a spectral survey carried out with ALMA in Band 6 (220.7$-$274.9 GHz). We identified about 3,700 molecular emission lines and discovered 23 COMs in the disk.

evidence.quote: V883 Ori is an eruptive young stellar object in transition between Class I and Class II, located within the Orion Molecular Cloud at a distance of 388 pc (cite: jelee19).
Its disk inclination is 38.3$^{\circ}$, and the mass of the protostar is 1.2 M$_{\odot}$ (cite: cieza_2016; jelee19).
V883 Ori is an eruptive young stellar object in transition between Class I and Class II, located within the Orion Molecular Cloud at a distance of 388 pc (cite: jelee19).
Its disk inclination is 38.3$^{\circ}$, and the mass of the protostar is 1.2 M$_{\odot}$ (cite: cieza_2016; jelee19).

question.value: What is the COM inventory and composition of the freshly sublimated ices in the Keplerian disk of the eruptive star V883 Ori, and how does it compare with hot corinos, hot cores and comet 67P?

evidence.quote: In this paper, we report the results of our COMs analyses with the V883 Ori spectral survey data, focusing on oxygen- and nitrogen-bearing species.
In the ALMA Cycle 7 program 2019.1.00377.S (PI: Jeong-Eun Lee), we performed an unbiased spectral survey of V883 Ori in Band 6
The frequency range covered by the spectral survey is 220.703 GHz to 274.861 GHz with a spectral resolution of 488.281 kHz (0.66$-$0.53 km s$^{-1}$).
with an angular resolution of 0.15$\ensuremath{''}$$-$0.2$\ensuremath{''}$, corresponding to $\sim$60 to 80 au at a distance of 388 pc
The continuum sensitivity is 0.01 mJy beam$^{-1}$, and the line sensitivity is 0.4$-$0.6 mJy beam$^{-1}$.
The on-source integration time is 194.5 minutes.
The observations were conducted between May 2021 and November 2021.
In the ALMA Cycle 7 program 2019.1.00377.S (PI: Jeong-Eun Lee)

what.value: Dust mass opacity kappa=2.2 cm2/g at 230 GHz and beta=1

evidence.quote: We adopt $\kappa_{\rm ref}= 2.2$ cm$^{2}$ g$^{-1}$ (at $\nu_{\rm ref}$= 230 GHz) and $\beta$=1 from (cite: Cieza2018).

what.value: Disk model average temperature 120 K within 0.3'' used as T_rot

evidence.quote: $T_{\rm rot}$ was set to 120 K, which is the average temperature within 0.3$\ensuremath{''}$ radius of the disk model of V883 Ori (cite: jelee19).

what.value: HDO:H2O ratio 2.26e-3 used to derive water column

evidence.quote: The water column density was calculated from our estimated HDO column density (6.68$\times$10$^{16}$ cm$^{-2}$) and the disk-averaged HDO:H$_{2}$O ratio (2.26$\times$10$^{-3}$) reported by (cite: Tobin2023).
For this comparison, we used the results of IRAS 16293-2422B in the IRAS 16293-2422 binary system.
Through the mission, various organic compounds were discovered, and their abundances were determined (cite: Schuhmann2019; Rubin2019).

continuum_subtraction.value: image-space subtraction, continuum level measured with STATCONT

evidence.quote: The continuum emission was subtracted in the image space, and the continuum level is automatically measured using `STATCONT` (cite: Sanchez-Monge2018).
The details of observation and data reduction can be found in (cite: jelee2024).
For more information, please refer to (cite: yun2023pca).

method.value: PC1 filtering of the data cube over the COM emission region

evidence.quote: We extracted averaged spectra over the entire COMs emission region in the disk ($\sim$0.3$''$) using a newly-developed filtering technique: first principal component (PC1) filtering method

method.value: Fit continuum vs spectral window weighted by PC1 moment 0 to get N_H2 and eta; divide line intensity by exp(-tau_dust)

evidence.quote: To get $N_{\rm H_{2}}$ and $\eta$, we fitted the continuum intensities as a function of spectral windows, weighted by the moment 0 map of the PC1

key_parameters.value: SG2 and SG3 spectra scaled up by 5% and 2%

evidence.quote: we scaled up the SG2 and SG3 spectra by 5% and 2%, respectively.

assumptions.value: Dust and gas coupled, gas in LTE; kappa=2.2 cm2/g at 230 GHz, beta=1

evidence.quote: We assume that dust and gas are well coupled and that the gas is in LTE.

method.value: XCLASS model spectra for ~1500 species at 35 column density steps; f_N,X = matched/modeled lines; keep species reaching 100%, then visual inspection

evidence.quote: for every possible species (about 1,500), we constructed model spectra with 35 column density steps (from 5$\times$10$^{12}$ cm$^{-2}$ to 5$\times$10$^{18}$ cm$^{-2}$).

key_parameters.value: v_width = 3 km/s, T_rot = 120 K, eta = 0.384, N free

evidence.quote: We fixed $v_{\rm width}$ at 3 km s$^{-1}$, which is obtained from the PC1-filtered spectrum.
Assuming local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE), `XCLASS` can model the spectra of each molecular species
Finally, we performed a visual inspection to confirm the detection of those molecules selected by this procedure.

analysis_steps.goal: Derive column densities by iterative LTE fitting

method.value: Fit N only with MAGIX, iteratively keeping isolated lines with tau<0.7 and width<4 km/s until convergence

evidence.quote: The optical depth criterion is set to $\tau_{\rm \nu,line}=0.7$, meaning that only lines with their modeled $\tau_{\rm \nu,line}$ lower than 0.7 are considered in the fitting process.

key_parameters.value: tau criterion 0.7; exclude line width >4 km/s

evidence.quote: we removed observed lines with large line width ($>$ 4 km s$^{-1}$), which may be due to blending with unidentified lines.
the column density ($N$) was the only free parameter in the analysis, while the other parameters were fixed to the aforementioned values.

fitting.value: Genetic algorithm for best fit; MCMC for uncertainties

evidence.quote: The genetic algorithm was used to derive the best-fit values of the parameters, and the Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) method was used to calculate the uncertainties.

validation.value: Rotation diagram comparison: scatter 0.28 dex, offset 0.03 dex

evidence.quote: the difference in column densities obtained from the two methods has a scatter of 0.28 dex with only a slight offset of 0.03 dex.

analysis_steps.goal: Upper limits and comparison with other sources

method.value: 3 sigma upper limits for nondetections; abundances relative to CH3OH compared with IRAS 16293B, comet 67P and other sources; 12C/13C ratios

evidence.quote: The column density producing the strongest line corresponding to the 3$\sigma$ level of the observation is considered the upper limit.
We used the eXtended CASA Line Analysis Software Suite (cite: Moller17) for the line identification.
We operated a fitting tool of `XCLASS`: the Modeling and Analysis Generic Interface for eXternal numerical codes (`MAGIX`) (cite: Moller13).
the continuum level is automatically measured using `STATCONT` (cite: Sanchez-Monge2018)
a total of 23 complex organic molecular species have been found in V883 Ori, based on about 3,700 lines above 3$\sigma$.
Finally, the fitted $\eta$ is 0.384, and the fitted $N_{\rm H_{2}}$ is $1.24\times10^{25}$ cm$^{-2}$ with uncertainty of 2$\%$.

findings_qualitative.value: Only CH3CN among nitrogen-bearing COMs is detected; CH2OH-bearing COMs are missing while O-bearing COMs are abundant

evidence.quote: nitrogen-bearing COMs other than CH$_{3}$CN are missing, whereas various oxygen-bearing COMs, except for the CH$_2$OH-bearing molecules, are detected.

claims.hypothesis: Does including optically thick lines bias COM column densities?
claims.experiment: Iterative LTE fitting with tau<0.7 versus fitting all lines
claims.result: All-line fits underestimate N for CH3OH, CH3OCHO, CH3CHO by up to nearly an order of magnitude
claims.finding: Using only optically thin lines over a wide frequency range is critical

evidence.quote: the latter method underestimates the column density by up to almost an order of magnitude compared to the former.

claims.hypothesis: Is the V883 Ori COM inventory like hot corinos?
claims.experiment: Compare abundances relative to CH3OH with IRAS 16293B and 67P
claims.result: Abundances higher than hot corino, comparable to comet; CH2OH- and N-bearing COMs missing
claims.finding: Possible in-disk chemical evolution and water-rich ice formation

evidence.quote: The higher abundances than the Class 0 hot corino and similar abundances with the cometary ices may indicate the possibility of in-situ chemical evolution in a disk

claims.hypothesis: Do COMs show carbon isotope fractionation?
claims.finding: Lower than local ISM and comet 67P

evidence.quote: The average $^{12}$C/$^{13}$C ratio estimated from various COMs detected in V883 Ori is 24.4

why_this_method.value: Wide unbiased coverage allows selecting isolated optically thin lines

evidence.quote: This approach using only optically thin, isolated lines is possible because we identified as many molecular lines as possible during the line identification process

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: T_rot of 200 K and 300 K rejected; 120 K fits most species best

evidence.quote: Above all, the spectra of most species are best fitted by 120 K.

limitations_admitted.value: Fixed beam-filling factor makes column densities likely lower limits (factor ~2-3)

evidence.quote: the accurate beam-filling factors of less abundant molecules can increase the column densities by a factor of $\sim2-3$, so the current values can be considered lower limits.
Most observed lines have been identified, but $\sim$20$\%$ of the lines remain unidentified.

referee_caveats_inferred: Single T_rot and eta for all species despite different emitting regions
Disk-averaged spectra ignore radial temperature structure
Dust correction assumes a single averaged tau
Nitrogen interpretation of ammonium salts is speculative
